translation.title: Ketoprofen Plaster
translation.efficacy: This medicine is used for pain relief and anti-inflammation in degenerative arthritis (osteoarthritis), periarthritis of the shoulder, tendinitis and tenosynovitis, peritendinitis, epicondylitis of the humerus (tennis elbow, etc.), muscle pain, and post-traumatic swelling and pain.
translation.usage: Remove the release liner from the adhesive side and apply the plaster to the affected area twice a day.
translation.caution: Do not use this medicine if you are or have been hypersensitive or photosensitive to it, if you have or have had aspirin-induced asthma (asthma attacks caused by non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, etc.), if you are hypersensitive to ingredients that can cause cross-hypersensitivity (tiaprofenic acid, fenofibrate, bezafibrate, ciprofibrate, oxybenzone), if you are 6 months or more pregnant, or for children under 15 years. Consult a doctor or pharmacist before use if you have bronchial asthma, or if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. While using this medicine and for up to 2 weeks after use, avoid outdoor activities regardless of the weather, and when you go out, cover the application site with clothing, sunglasses, a hat, sunscreen, etc. so that it is not exposed to ultraviolet light. Do not use it on the eyes or mucous membranes, on damaged skin or mucous membranes, on areas with eczema or rash, or on athlete's foot or ringworm (tinea). Do not use it under an occlusive dressing. Adverse reactions may occur - rarely shock (hives, difficulty breathing, facial swelling and other hypersensitivity-like symptoms) and asthma attacks (dry crackles, wheezing, difficulty breathing); sometimes contact dermatitis with redness, rash, itching, blisters, oozing, irritation and swelling, dry skin and pigmentation, and photosensitivity caused by direct sunlight; if any of these occur, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. Store at room temperature away from light, and keep out of reach of children.
